identity.title: From Exploration to Mastery: Enabling LLMs to Master Tools via Self-Driven Interactions

problem.claim: The paper addresses how LLMs can better comprehend and use external tools through tool documentation.

gap.claim: Existing human-centric tool documentation is described as inadequate and inaccurate, creating a comprehension gap between LLMs and external tools.

contributions.claim: The authors propose DRAFT, which dynamically refines tool documentation using feedback and trials from LLM–tool interactions.
DRAFT uses iterative experience gathering, learning from experience, and documentation rewriting, with diversity-promoting exploration and tool-adaptive termination.
The authors report improved documentation quality, tool comprehension, and tool utilization, along with robust cross-model generalization of refined documentation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe DRAFT as a novel framework for dynamically refining tool documentation from LLM interaction feedback and trials.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments across multiple datasets found DRAFT’s iterative, feedback-based refinement improved documentation quality and supported more effective tool use.
The authors report that documentation refined by DRAFT showed robust cross-model generalization.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tool learning can extend LLM interaction with external environments, while documentation guides tool use.
The paper identifies inadequate and inaccurate human-centric documentation as a source of LLM–tool comprehension mismatch.
DRAFT refines documentation from interaction feedback through three iterative learning phases.
DRAFT adds diversity-promoting exploration and tool-adaptive termination for exploration diversity, efficiency, and overfitting prevention.
Experiments reportedly show better documentation and tool use, with cross-model generalization of refined documentation.

source_observation.claim: The paper links documentation rewriting to accumulated interaction experience and explicitly separates experience gathering, learning, and rewriting phases.

lessons.interpretation: A staged pipeline can make the path from behavioral feedback to revised instructions explicit and inspectable.
lessons.application: Describe an adaptive-instruction method as separate data collection, feedback interpretation, and artifact-revision stages, and state what each stage consumes and produces.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the system cannot obtain interaction feedback or when documentation is fixed by external governance.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs exploration diversity with a tool-adaptive stopping mechanism and reports cross-model generalization as an outcome.

lessons.interpretation: Resource-control mechanisms and transfer behavior can be presented as integral design concerns rather than afterthoughts.
lessons.application: When proposing self-improvement through trials, specify both how exploration is diversified and how termination adapts to the tool, then report transfer across models if evaluated.
lessons.exception: Cross-model transfer is not a meaningful target when the artifact is deliberately model-specific.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, effect sizes, or statistical conditions behind the reported improvements.
The mechanism and evaluation details supporting the claimed cross-model generalization are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the proposed method’s effectiveness or novelty.
